types.name: ConsumerBatchContext
types.summary: What the loop knows at the end of a page, handed to `onBatch`.

fields.name: cursor
fields.description: Checkpoint to commit alongside your rows.

fields.name: height
fields.description:
Highest canonical block a row was DELIVERED from. `null` before the
first row of a fresh consume. With a sparse filter this parks at the
last matching event — it measures event recency, not progress.

fields.name: scannedHeight
fields.description:
Highest canonical block the sweep has VERIFIED through: an empty page
is the server confirming nothing matches between the cursor and the
tip, so a caught-up tail scans to the tip even when `height` is far
below it. Rolls back with reorg rewinds.

fields.name: tipHeight
fields.description: Chain tip as of this page's read.

fields.name: blocksBehind
fields.description:
`tipHeight - scannedHeight`, floored at 0 — the consumer's actual
backlog. `null` until a position is known. A caught-up consumer on a
quiet contract reads ~0 here while `tipHeight - height` grows — that
difference is event age, not lag.

fields.name: tip
fields.description:
The full tip for this page — `StreamsTip` or `IndexTip` depending on the
surface. Exposed here so a handler never needs the `envelope` parameter,
which is the only way to reach it today and is also how the worst
`finalizedOnly` mistake becomes reachable (`return envelope.next_cursor`
jumps the cursor past events that were filtered out and never delivered).

fields.name: reorgs
fields.description:
Reorgs reported alongside this page; empty when none. Rollback still
belongs in `onReorg` — this is for observability inside a batch.

types.name: ConsumerSink
types.summary: A consumer sink: the destination adapter a consume loop writes through.

fields.name: _tx
fields.description:
Phantom marker carrying `Tx` in a directly-inferable position, so the
consume loops' `TTx` type parameter resolves from the `sink` option
(never set at runtime).

fields.name: capabilities
fields.description:
Static capabilities, read by the loop before the first fetch to fail
fast on impossible pairings.

fields.name: loadCursor
fields.description:
The committed checkpoint, or `null` on first run. Called once, before
the first page. Implementations may create their checkpoint storage
here and SHOULD validate their rollback preconditions (e.g. that every
declared table carries the height column).

fields.name: commitBatch
fields.type: (cursor: string, write: (tx: Tx) => Promise<null> | null) => Promise<null>
fields.description:
Apply one batch atomically: open a transaction, run `write(tx)` (the
user's inserts), and commit the rows AND `cursor` together. A throw
from `write` must abort the whole transaction — leaving neither rows
nor cursor, so a crashed batch is simply re-read on restart.

fields.name: rollback
fields.description:
Roll the projection back to the fork: delete everything AT OR ABOVE
`forkPointHeight` (inclusive `>=` — the new chain re-supplies the fork
block) and commit `rewindCursor` in the SAME transaction. Deleting
without the rewound cursor is the classic silent-gap bug: a crash
between the two writes resumes above the fork and the deleted range is
never re-read.

On a multi-fork page this is called once PER fork, every call with the
same `rewindCursor` (the lowest fork point) but its own
`forkPointHeight` — scope the undo by `forkPointHeight` only (contract
invariant #11), and expect re-application after a crash (#10).

`rewindCursor` is `null` only for a fork at genesis: clear the
checkpoint so the next run starts from the first event.

fields.name: sender
fields.description: tx-sender (the signer). `null` when the VM had none.

fields.name: caller
fields.description: The contract that issued `contract-call?`.

fields.name: function_args
fields.description: Clarity hex per argument.

fields.name: raw_value
fields.description: Canonical serialized hex of `value`, when the stream carries it.

types.name: RuneEtchEntry
types.summary: The etch a `rune_etch` event created — everything a consumer needs to render a fresh rune without a second lookup, minus what the envelope already carries (`rune_id`).

fields.name: name
fields.description: No spacers, uppercase.

fields.name: spaced_name
fields.description: As etched, spacers included (e.g. `DOG•GO•TO•THE•MOON`).

fields.name: premine
fields.description: u128 decimal string. Never `Number()`.

fields.name: terms
fields.type: { amount: string | null; cap: string | null; height_start: string | null; height_end: string | null; offset_start: string | null; offset_end: string | null; } | null

fields.name: amount
fields.description: u128 decimal string. Never `Number()`.

fields.name: vout
fields.description:
The output this event landed on. Set on `rune_transfer` only — an etch
or mint's allocation isn't tied to one output the way a transfer is
(`packages/bitcoin/src/runes/updater.ts`).

fields.name: address
fields.description:
The output's mainnet address. Set on `rune_transfer` only, and only
when the output has a standard scriptPubKey.

fields.name: entry
fields.description: `rune_etch` only — the entry this event created.

fields.name: ts
fields.description:
The event's block time, ISO 8601. Absent when the indexer has no header
time for that block yet (rows written before block times were recorded,
until backfilled).

fields.name: finalized
fields.description:
True when this event's block is past the finality boundary (immutable).
Optional for back-compat with the same reasoning as `StreamsEventBase`.

types.name: StreamsEvent
types.summary: A raw Streams event.
types.definition: StreamsEventOf<"stx_transfer", StxTransferPayload> | StreamsEventOf<"stx_mint", StxMintPayload> | StreamsEventOf<"stx_burn", StxBurnPayload> | StreamsEventOf<"stx_lock", StxLockPayload> | StreamsEventOf<"ft_transfer", FtTransferPayload> | StreamsEventOf<"ft_mint", FtMintPayload> | StreamsEventOf<"ft_burn", FtBurnPayload> | StreamsEventOf<"nft_transfer", NftTransferPayload> | StreamsEventOf<"nft_mint", NftMintPayload> | StreamsEventOf<"nft_burn", NftBurnPayload> | StreamsEventOf<"print", PrintPayload>

fields.name: cursor
fields.description:
Globally unique, monotonic position of this event (`<block>:<index>`). Use
it as the primary key of your projection rows — replaying a batch then
upserts cleanly. Don't synthesize your own id from `tx_id`/`event_index`.

fields.name: finalized
fields.description:
True when this event's block is past the finality boundary (immutable).
Optional for back-compat; the API always sets it on Streams responses.

fields.name: matched
fields.description:
Labels whose filter group this event satisfied, present only when the
request used a labelled `filters` map. The SDK dispatches on it for you
(`on.<label>`), so handlers rarely read it directly.

fields.name: chain
fields.description:
Which chain this event came from (plan 059). Every Stacks Streams
response sets this to `"stacks"`; optional here for back-compat with
fixtures/tests that pre-date the field — the same reasoning as
`finalized?`. Cursors stay per-chain but chain-agnostic in shape, so this
is the only signal a mixed-chain caller can discriminate on.

types.name: StreamsEventsConsumeBitcoinParams
types.summary: `chain: "bitcoin"` (plan 059/061) — the checkpointed sweep over Runes events.

fields.name: rune
fields.description: A RuneRef: an id (`840000:3`) or a name (`DOG•GO•TO•THE•MOON`).

fields.name: address
fields.description: A mainnet address.

fields.name: onBatch
fields.type: (events: RuneStreamsEvent[], envelope: StreamsEventsEnvelope<RuneStreamsEvent, StreamsBitcoinTip>, ctx: StreamsBatchContext & [TTx] extends [never] ? unknown : { tx: TTx }) => string | Promise<null> | Promise<string | undefined | null> | undefined | null

fields.name: onError
fields.type: (err: unknown, ctx: { attempt: number; retriesLeft: number; delayMs: number }) => null

fields.name: chain
fields.description:
`chain: "stacks"` (default, omit `chain` entirely) — the bitcoin branch
is 
[`StreamsEventsConsumeBitcoinParams`](/docs/sdk-reference/streams#t-StreamsEventsConsumeBitcoinParams)
, a separate overload with
no `filters`/`on`/`decoded` (Stacks-only concepts).

fields.name: decoded
fields.description:
Deliver events pre-decoded as the flat, `event_type`-discriminated rows
Index serves (`IndexEvent`), so Streams consumption reads identically
to Index consumption — no guard+decode pairs in your handler.

fields.name: onProgress
fields.description: Fires once per page, before `onBatch` and before any early return.

fields.name: finalizedOnly
fields.description:
Emit only finalized (immutable) events and never surface reorgs. The SDK
checkpoints at the last finalized event and re-reads the unfinalized tail
until it settles. Trades finality lag for zero reorg handling; `onReorg` is
ignored.

fields.name: filters
fields.description:
Labelled filter groups. The groups OR together in ONE server-side scan,
so two unrelated concerns share one page, one cursor, and one checkpoint
instead of two consume loops. Pair with `on` to handle each label.

fields.name: on
fields.type: { [K in keyof F]: ( events: StreamsEventForFilter<F[K], D>[], ctx: StreamsBatchContext & WithSinkTx<TTx>, ) => void | Promise<void>; }
fields.description:
One handler per label in `filters`. Every label must be handled, so
adding a label is a compile error until its handler exists.

A label's declared `types` narrows its handler's events, so `payload` is
typed without an `event_type` guard. Labels are dispatched in declaration
order: a label's own events stay in cursor order, but events of different
labels do not interleave within a page — add `onBatch` when you need
strict global order across labels.

fields.name: onBatch
fields.type: (events: D extends true ? IndexEvent[] : StreamsEvent[], envelope: StreamsEventsEnvelope<StreamsEvent, StreamsTip>, ctx: StreamsBatchContext & [TTx] extends [never] ? unknown : { tx: TTx }) => string | Promise<null> | Promise<string | undefined | null> | undefined | null
fields.description:
Apply a page of canonical events. Persist `ctx.cursor` in the same
transaction as your writes. Returning a cursor overrides `ctx.cursor` as
the resume point (advanced manual control); returning nothing uses it.

Optional only when `on` handles the page instead; a consume call with
neither throws.

fields.name: onReorg
fields.description:
Roll your projection back to `reorg.fork_point_height`, persisting
`ctx.cursor` in the same transaction. Called once per *new* reorg at or
below the checkpoint (deduped in-memory, fork-ascending) before the SDK
rewinds and re-reads the now-canonical events. A reorg whose fork sits
above the checkpoint is not a rollback (nothing past it was written) and
is skipped. Omit it to ignore reorgs (events stay canonical, but stale
rows from an orphaned fork are left in place).

With `onReorg` or a `sink` attached, every empty page also polls
`reorgs.list` (one extra request per idle poll) so a fork that lands
while the consumer idles at the tip is rolled back too.

fields.name: maxRollbackDepth
fields.description:
Deepest rewind one reorg may make below the checkpoint before the loop
refuses with `ValidationError`. Default 1000 blocks. The fork point is
server supplied and drives a delete on every declared table, so raise
this only for a source you trust.

fields.name: retryCount
fields.description:
Page-fetch retries after the first failure (429/5xx/network only —
4xx and handler throws always propagate). Default 3; `0` disables.

fields.name: retryDelay
fields.description:
Base retry delay in ms; the n-th retry waits `retryDelay * n`. A server
`Retry-After` overrides it. Default 1000.

fields.name: onError
fields.type: (err: unknown, ctx: { attempt: number; retriesLeft: number; delayMs: number }) => null
fields.description: Void observer, called before each retry sleep (metrics/logging).

fields.name: wake
fields.description:
Cuts the empty-poll backoff short: on an empty page, the loop races
`emptyBackoffMs` against this promise instead of sleeping the full
amount. Pass a function that resolves once when new data MIGHT be
available (e.g. a Postgres NOTIFY listener) — it is called fresh on
every empty page, never awaited more than once concurrently per page.
The backoff timer still runs underneath, so a wake source that never
resolves (or a `wake` this call omits) degrades to the same polling
behavior as before.

fields.name: from
fields.description: Start point: `"genesis"` (default) or a `<block>:<index>` cursor.

fields.name: onDumpFile
fields.type: (file: StreamsDumpFile, ctx: { from: string | null }) => Promise<null> | null
fields.description:
Called once per finalized dump file, in block order, before live tailing.
Process the parquet with your own tooling (e.g. DuckDB) — the SDK does not
decode parquet. Use `client.dumps.download(file)` to fetch + verify bytes.

Delivery is file-granular and at-least-once: a file whose range straddles
`from` is handed over whole. `ctx.from` is that cursor (`null` from
genesis); skip rows at or below it, or key rows by `cursor` so a re-run
is an idempotent no-op. Files ending at or below `from` are not handed
over at all.

fields.name: onBatch
fields.type: (events: StreamsEvent[], envelope: StreamsEventsEnvelope<StreamsEvent, StreamsTip>) => string | Promise<string | undefined | null> | undefined | null
fields.description: Called per live page after the dump phase, like `consume`.

fields.name: onReorg
fields.description:
Called when the live-tail phase (after the dump backfill) crosses a reorg,
before the cursor rewinds and re-reads the now-canonical events — same
contract as `consume`. The dump-backfill phase is finalized and never
reorgs; omit this to leave stale rows from an orphaned fork in place.

fields.name: types
fields.description:
Narrow the LIVE TAIL after the dump phase. The dump files themselves are
always all-type (block-partitioned parquet) — filter those in your own
tooling while processing each file.

fields.name: filters
fields.description: Labelled OR-groups for the live tail, like `consume`.

fields.description: Event types to exclude (applied after `types`).

fields.name: filters
fields.description:
Labelled filter groups. The groups OR together in one scan and each

types.name: StreamsEventsSubscribeBitcoinParams
types.summary: `chain: "bitcoin"` (plan 059/061) — Runes events pushed live, on their own cursor space.

fields.name: fromCursor
fields.description: Resume strictly after this cursor; omit to live-tail from the tip.

fields.name: onError
fields.description:
Called on every failure. Transport errors (dropped socket, 5xx, 429, a
stale connection, a throwing handler) reconnect from the last handled
cursor with exponential backoff. Errors that a retry cannot fix (401,
4xx, a bad signature) end the subscription and reject its `done`.

fields.name: reconnectDelayMs
fields.description:
First reconnect pause in ms (default 1000). Doubles per consecutive
failure up to 30 s with jitter, resets once a frame arrives, and never
undercuts a `Retry-After`.

fields.name: staleAfterMs
fields.description:
Reconnect when no frame (pings included) arrives for this long (default
60000, three server heartbeats). Catches a half-open socket that never
errors; set it above your instance's heartbeat interval.

fields.name: rune
fields.description: A RuneRef: an id (`840000:3`) or a name (`DOG•GO•TO•THE•MOON`).

fields.name: address
fields.description: A mainnet address.

types.name: StreamsEventsSubscribeStacksParams
types.summary: `chain: "stacks"` (default, omit `chain` entirely).

fields.name: fromCursor
fields.description: Resume strictly after this cursor; omit to live-tail from the tip.

fields.name: onError
fields.description:
Called on every failure. Transport errors (dropped socket, 5xx, 429, a
stale connection, a throwing handler) reconnect from the last handled
cursor with exponential backoff. Errors that a retry cannot fix (401,
4xx, a bad signature) end the subscription and reject its `done`.

fields.name: reconnectDelayMs
fields.description:
First reconnect pause in ms (default 1000). Doubles per consecutive
failure up to 30 s with jitter, resets once a frame arrives, and never
undercuts a `Retry-After`.

fields.name: staleAfterMs
fields.description:
Reconnect when no frame (pings included) arrives for this long (default
60000, three server heartbeats). Catches a half-open socket that never
errors; set it above your instance's heartbeat interval.

fields.name: filters
fields.description:
Labelled filter groups; see 
`StreamsEventsListParams.filters`
.

fields.name: onEvent
fields.description:
Called for each pushed event, in order. The resume cursor advances only
after this resolves, so a handler that throws sees the same event again
on reconnect (at-least-once). Key durable writes by `cursor`.

fields.name: new_canonical_tip
fields.description:
First position of the new canonical chain at the fork, `fork:0`
(INCLUSIVE). Not an exclusive resume token — resuming directly from it
skips `fork:0`. The consumer rewinds to the foot of `fork_point_height`
(`Cursor.atHeight`) to re-read the new run from `fork:0` inclusive.

types.name: StreamsReorgContext
types.summary: `cursor` is the rewind position the loop resumes from after `onReorg`: the foot of the fork point, or `null` for a fork at genesis.

types.name: StreamsSubscription
types.summary: Handle for a live subscription: call it to unsubscribe.

fields.name: finalized_height
fields.description:
Highest Stacks block past the burn-confirmation finality boundary.
Optional for back-compat; the API always sets it.

fields.name: oldest_seekable_height
fields.description:
Oldest height still seekable on the live API for the caller's tier
(`tip - retention`). `null` = unlimited retention. Older reads must use the
cold dumps lane. Optional for back-compat.

fields.name: oldest_cursor
fields.description: Oldest seekable cursor (`<oldest_seekable_height>:0`); `null` = unlimited.

types.name: StreamsWireEvent
types.summary: Anything `GET /v1/streams/events` can return: Streams 1.0 rows on the classic clock, vm rows on `clock=vm`, or Runes rows on `chain=bitcoin`.

types.name: VmStreamsEvent
types.summary: A Streams `clock=vm` row.
types.definition: VmStreamsEventOf<"nested_contract_call", NestedContractCallPayload> | VmStreamsEventOf<"var_set", VarSetPayload> | VmStreamsEventOf<"map_set", MapWritePayload> | VmStreamsEventOf<"map_insert", MapWritePayload> | VmStreamsEventOf<"map_delete", MapDeletePayload>

fields.name: cursor
fields.description:
Globally unique, monotonic position of this event (`<block>:<index>`). Use
it as the primary key of your projection rows — replaying a batch then
upserts cleanly. Don't synthesize your own id from `tx_id`/`event_index`.

fields.name: finalized
fields.description:
True when this event's block is past the finality boundary (immutable).
Optional for back-compat; the API always sets it on Streams responses.

fields.name: matched
fields.description:
Labels whose filter group this event satisfied, present only when the
request used a labelled `filters` map. The SDK dispatches on it for you
(`on.<label>`), so handlers rarely read it directly.

fields.name: chain
fields.description:
Which chain this event came from (plan 059). Every Stacks Streams
response sets this to `"stacks"`; optional here for back-compat with
fixtures/tests that pre-date the field — the same reasoning as
`finalized?`. Cursors stay per-chain but chain-agnostic in shape, so this
is the only signal a mixed-chain caller can discriminate on.
